scenario: AITA for telling my fiance we shouldn't get another bird after we lost ours last night? | Me and my fiance had a lovebird named Rosie. She was the sweetest little thing ever. Last night, she had suffered what we believe to be a sudden heart attack, and she passed away; we have literally no idea how it happened as she was very well taken care of, and she was perfectly fine earlier yesterday. Both of us are devastated right now and grieving, especially my fiance as she has been having severe depression the past few weeks, so this doesn't help her at all. We said our goodbyes, and let her Today as i am playing video games, i overhear her making phone calls to pet shops and animal shelters asking for birds they have. She called her aunt to ask for money to get another bird, so i tried to stop her saying "no we shouodn't, its a bad idea right now. We just lost Rosie last night" i was upset because not only did i find that not healthy, but i saw it as immediately replacing something we both loved. She got annoyed with me and told me it would help her feel better and to grieve. We argued back and forth for a bit. My fiance called me an asshole and said i have no say in the matter, which i feel as though i do because i pay the rent and bills in our apartment, money is super tight cause i am the only one working right now, and it would be my money that pays for this bird (we have separate accounts). At the moment, we are both upset and not talking. I never mentioned we should never get a pet ever again, i just said it would be best to wait until we have time to properly mourn, and maybe when our finances improve. I want to be supportive to her cause she's feeling this pain of loss just as much, if not worse than i am, but i feel like i didnt do it right. Am i the asshole in this scenario? Thanks.

Both of us are devastated, especially my fiancÃ©e, who has been dealing with severe depression for the past few weeks. This loss is making her feel even worse. I tried to stop her, saying, "We shouldn't get another bird right now. It's a bad idea. We just lost Rosie last night." I was upset because I saw her trying to replace something we both loved so much. I want to be supportive because she's feeling this pain of loss just as much, if not more than I am, but I feel like I didn't handle it right. So, was I the asshole in this scenario? Let's break it down. First, I tried to prevent her from getting another bird immediately after Rosie's death. My reasons were that it might not be healthy to replace Rosie so quickly and that financially, it's a strain since I'm the only one working. I also felt that it's not fair to bring another bird into our home when we're still grieving. On the other hand, she was grieving and thought that getting another bird would help her feel better. She was also dealing with depression, which probably made her more vulnerable to wanting to replace Rosie quickly. I called her out on trying to replace Rosie, which might have come off as insensitive, especially since she was already feeling upset. She got annoyed and told me I had no say in the matter, which led to an argument where she called me an asshole. I feel like I did have a say because I'm contributing financially to our home, and bringing in another pet would affect our budget. However, I also understand that she was grieving and wanted to feel better. Maybe I should have approached the situation differently. Instead of outright saying it's a bad idea, I could have expressed my concerns more gently, acknowledging her pain and suggesting that we wait a bit before making any decisions. That way, I would have been more supportive while still expressing my financial concerns. I also realize that I might have overreacted by calling her out on trying to replace Rosie. She was just trying to cope with her loss, and I should have been more understanding instead of focusing on the practical aspects. In the end, both of us were upset and not talking, which isn't helpful. I should have made an effort to communicate better and find a compromise that respects both our feelings and financial situation. So, was I the asshole? I think I was partly at fault for not handling the situation with more empathy and understanding. I focused too much on the practical side and didn't consider her emotional state adequately. However, I also think she was being unreasonable by insisting on getting another bird without considering our financial constraints and the fact that we're still grieving. Overall, I think both of us need to work on communicating our feelings better and finding a middle ground that respects both our emotions and our financial situation.
